title: Abhayagiri Dagaba, Anuradhapura
summary: The Abhayagiri dagaba at Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka is a great stupa attributed to King Vattagamani Abhaya (Valagamba), built on the site of a hermitage. A museum record gives 88 BC for its building and also a later date of 103 AD. A newspaper reports its height as 113 m originally and 75 m later.

uncertainty.note: The Victoria and Albert Museum record gives two dates: 88 BC (Dipavamsa) and 'commonly believed' 103 AD. Daily FT gives the king's second reign as 89-77 BC. Start -87 is 88 BC. The plus margin reaches 103 AD. End is the present.

reviewer_note: No model: no UNESCO, heritage-body, museum or scholarly page opened gives the dagaba's height or diameter; the 113 m and 75 m figures are from a newspaper, and the OSM outline tool failed (502) on this structure. The building date is contested: the V&A record gives 88 BC and 103 AD, and the Daily FT gives only the king's reign. The UNESCO documents for Anuradhapura opened have no dimensions.
